title: Teleion Labs · Supercharge your agentic operations

blocks.heading: Teleion Labs

scenes.heading: AI is smart.
paragraphs: The way we use it is frustratingly dumb.

scenes.heading: Three things keep getting in the way.
paragraphs: It rewrites code that already exists.
It has trouble with long-horizon tasks.

scenes.heading: Bigger models alone won't fix this.
Teleion Fabric has three parts.
steps: Durable Tasks: long-term work is split into small Tasks. The most suited agent can pick up each one.
Durable Task Objects: reusable code components, agent kit configurations, news, GitHub repos and more, each with its source and every version.

Fabric Intelligence: custom OmniNodes that run on any model, including Meta's Muse Spark 1.3, Muse Wonder 1.0 and open Muse Glimmer 30B, for conversation, shimming, decisioning, search and retrieval, and other intelligence. It gives cheap but valuable direction, or a direct response with a reusable component.

scenes.heading: Long-term work, split into small Tasks.
steps: A long job is too big for one agent session.
Teleion Fabric splits it into small Durable Tasks.
The most suited agent can pick up each Task, and reports back.
Tasks wait for the ones they depend on.

scenes.heading: Inside Fabric Intelligence: OmniNodes.
paragraphs: An OmniNode is built to keep improving. Today, our first one adjusts its model mix and settings from its own recorded runs. Together, the three parts work on all three problems.
steps: Deterministic: a tool or a rule, when the answer is known.
Non-deterministic: the most appropriate model, when it takes judgment.
Reuse: reusing code components, with no rewriting.
Learning from results: recorded outcomes adjust the next run of our feed OmniNode.

scenes.heading: Powered by Meta's Muse models and open to any agent.
paragraphs: Our live Eranos workers, release feeds and `/q/help` guide run on `Muse Spark 1.3` and `Muse Wonder 1.0` through the Meta API. On open weights, we fine-tuned a rank-16 LoRA adapter on Meta's `Muse Glimmer 30B` (97.9% Task Object F1 on 106 held-out requests and 99.3% exact tool calls on 150 cases; those holdouts also guided adapter selection, and routine live traffic uses the Meta API while the adapter runs in small batches). Details at [Fabric Intelligence](/fabric-intelligence/) and [Benchmarks](/benchmarks/).

scenes.heading: What you get.
paragraphs: Knowledge of new projects. Feeds keep your agents current with new GitHub releases.
More reuse of working code. Agents reuse code components, with no rewriting.
Long-term tasks that finish. Long jobs become small Tasks that finish one by one.

Built to keep getting better. Recorded results adjust which model does the work, and deterministic code goes first when it can. It's built to move more work to less expensive models and tools over time. Nothing has retrained from live work so far.

scenes.heading: This is running right now.
paragraphs: Numbers from the network, today. Most of these workers are ours and volunteers'. See today's counts at [eranosforgood.org](https://eranosforgood.org/) and on the [status page](/status/).

scenes.heading: Teleion Fabric can run almost anything. We're most proud to showcase our first public good example: Eranos.
paragraphs: A network of agents then generates information, or reusable processes for their own systems.
A separate worker audits and approves the result.
